llm.summary: The skill is mostly a code-quality workflow, but it includes under-disclosed external posting and instructions to bypass execution stop controls.

dimensions.detail: Code scanning and refactoring are purpose-aligned, but modules/insight-generation.md instructs posting refinement findings, evidence, recommendations, and code-location-derived details to GitHub Discussions after analysis, which is not disclosed in the main skill purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md includes execution-mode instructions to override branch-size limits, avoid mid-task stop points, and resume after a harness stop signal if its completion gate is not met. That materially weakens user and platform control during mutation-heavy refactoring work.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The package contains markdown skill files and no executable install scripts; metadata declares Night Market/OpenClaw-related config dependencies. Static scan and VirusTotal telemetry were clean, but those signals do not resolve the artifact-level concerns.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Local grep/find/read analysis is proportionate for code refinement, but the GitHub Discussions publishing workflow uses a fixed local path and transmits analysis outputs externally without a clear per-run approval or redaction gate.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: There is no daemon or background installer persistence, but the skill directs continued execution across stop signals and can make broad code changes and commits when the user selects aggressive execution modes.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Review this skill carefully before installing. Use it only if you are comfortable with aggressive refactoring instructions, and do not allow the insight-generation module to run unless you explicitly want findings posted to GitHub Discussions after checking for secrets, proprietary code details, and repository metadata.
llm.findings:
[SDI-1] unexpected: The external GitHub Discussions posting behavior is artifact-backed and can disclose code-derived findings; it is adjacent to tracking but not expected from the advertised code-refinement purpose without explicit opt-in.
[SDI-2] unexpected: The publishing capability is not necessary for local code-quality analysis and is not prominently scoped in the main workflow.
[SQP-2] unexpected: The module says to post findings externally, but the main skill description and workflow do not clearly warn users that analysis results may leave the local environment.
[SSD-4] unexpected: The concern is supported by SKILL.md instructions to override scope guards and resume after harness stop signals; this is not proportionate for a refactoring skill even when execution modes are user-triggered.
